analysis.summary: Thangamayil Jewellery Limited reported strong financial and operational performance for the financial year 2025-26, driven by organic growth, new retail outlets including in Chennai metro, and a high customer advance base. Revenue reached Rs. 84,933 lakhs, EBITDA stood at Rs. 57,674 lakhs, and PAT improved significantly to Rs. 35,165 lakhs.

demand_outlook.claim: Management noted that gold price increases act as a catalyst for savings and safe haven bets.
demand_outlook.quote: Elevated gold price will act as a catalyst both for savings and also as a safe heaven bet in an inflated economy

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA as a percentage of revenue for 2025-26 was reported at 6.79%.

orders_capacity.claim: The company's total operational retail space increased by 17.46% to reach 1,04,000 sq. ft.
orders_capacity.quote: Retail Space (increases by 17.46%) 104000 sq ft 88000 sq ft 18%

management_commitments.claim: The company plans to increase its customer base to 40 lakhs by March 31, 2026.
management_commitments.quote: Excellent Customer base built over period of years up to 32 Lakhs numbers and slated to increase to 40 Lakhs by 31/03/26

management_commitments.claim: The company plans to open the flagship Chennai outlet by January 2025.
management_commitments.quote: To open flagship Chennai outlet by Jan 2025.

management_commitments.claim: The company aims to complete geographical expansion in an additional 9 outlets as approved by the Board.
management_commitments.quote: To complete geographical expansion in additional 9 outlets as approved by the Board.

management_commitments.claim: The management targets to improve the gross profit margin from 9.64% to 10% on price rationalisation.
management_commitments.quote: Improve the gross profit margin from 9.64% to 10% on price rationalisation.

management_commitments.claim: The management aims to improve stock turnaround from 3.52 times to 3.75 times.
management_commitments.quote: Improve the stock turnaround from 3.52 times to 3.75 times.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
